{{Quote|Eh, so you had a bit of a rough landing, I think. Too bad for you, eh? New ships don't come cheap.|Watto to the spacer|<ref name="JGG" />}}
At some point before [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], a '''starship''' belonging to an [[Extragalactic/Legends|extra-galactic]] [[Unidentified extra-galactic spacer|spacer]] was forced to land on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] after colliding with an [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroid]] of the [[Dragon's Spine (asteroid field)|Dragon's Spine]] [[Asteroid field/Legends|belt]]. Because of the accident, the starship was heavily damaged, but its owner managed to gather enough local [[Wupiupi/Legends|Wupiupi credits]] to buy new parts and rebuild it. Following its refitting, the ship was equipped with a [[StarMark III Hyperdrive]] bought from [[Watto/Legends|Watto]], a [[Junk dealer/Legends|junk dealer]] from the [[Mos Espa/Legends|Mos Espa]] [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]].

==Description==
{{Quote|This checklist should help you to decide which parts to buy next, huh?|Watto to the spacer|<ref name="JGG" />}}
[[File:Checklist_SWMath.png|thumb|left|200px|The damaged ship's blueprints and checklist]]
Before its crash-landing on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], that [[Starship/Legends|starship]] of [[Extragalactic/Legends|extra-galactic]] origins was equipped with a quadruple-thruster propulsion system, a pair of delta wings and a [[Hull/Legends|hull]] that looked very much like the [[T-06 hull]] manufactured by [[Incom Corporation/Legends|Incom Corporation]]. For the most part, the ship was painted in a standard gray [[Color/Legends|hue]], although the wings, tails and outer cockpit bore distinctive crimson markings.<ref name="JGG" />

However, following its forced landing, the ship was heavily damaged, and it became necessary to rebuild it from scratch with components available on Tatooine. After an extensive refitting that cost between 3,829 and 6,329 [[Wupiupi/Legends|wupiupi]], the ship was equipped with a [[StarMark III Hyperdrive|StarMark III]] [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] for [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] travel, three [[Voyager III]] [[Fuel cell/Legends|fuel cells]] to store more energy, three [[GalaxyGuard Mk. VII]] [[Shield booster/Legends|shield boosters]] to increase the [[Deflector shield/Legends|deflector shield's]] power, and three [[Polestar subZero]] [[blaster radiator]]s to better dissipate the heat in the ship's mounted weapons. Additionally, the craft was given a brand new paint job.<ref name="JGG" />

{{GameMechanics|legends=1}}
In addition to the above, the starship also had to replace its original hull, its engine types, and its wings, with the spacer having chosen either the [[Slipstream IV hull]], the T-06 hull, or the [[AeroMaster XI hull]]; the [[Sun-Gull 1e wing]], the [[StarWind V wing]], or the [[Nebula 3 wing]] sets; and the [[Thornley Space Systems]]-developed [[NovaFury MonoThruster]]s, the [[Galaxy Seven]], or the [[Hamilton Engineering]]-developed [[Delta-C Tri-Thruster]]s.<ref name="JGG" />
{{Endgame}}

==History==
At some point before the [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]] [[Boonta Eve Classic (32 BBY)/Legends|edition]] of the [[Boonta Eve Classic/Legends|Boonta Eve Classic]],<ref name="Timeline" /> an [[Extragalactic/Legends|extra-galactic]] [[Unidentified extra-galactic spacer|spacer]] ventured in the [[Dragon's Spine (asteroid field)|Dragon's Spine]], an [[Asteroid field/Legends|asteroid field]] of the [[Tatoo system/Legends|Tatoo system]], with his or her ship. Upon entering the field, the spacecraft collided with an [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroid]], causing it to enter a spin and crash on the closest planet, Tatooine. Reaching the [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Mos Espa/Legends|Mos Espa]], the spacer encountered [[Watto/Legends|Watto]], a local [[Junk dealer/Legends|junk dealer]] who offered to sell him ship parts to repair the heavily damagaed craft. Bereft of money, the marooned spacer visited [[Jabba's Game Plaza]], a gaming venue in which local [[Wupiupi/Legends|Wupiupi credits]] could be gained.<ref name="JGG" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Final_ship_Jabba_math.png|200px|thumb|A possible canon depiction of the repaired ship]]
That unidentified starship appeared in the [[2000]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars Math: Jabba's Game Galaxy]]'', released by [[Lucas Learning]]. Using wupiupi credits earned in the various activities of the game, the player could collect parts and pieces used in the rebuilding of his crashed spaceship. Because of that, the final appearance of the starship depends on the player's choice. However, the game still contained a hint of what the [[canon]]ical ship may have looked like following the repairs. The map of Mos Espa featured a "fly ship" icon thanks to which the player could leave Tatooine and end the game. The icon featured a starship clearly made of an AeroMaster XI hull, a Delta-C Tri-Thruster and a Nebula 3 wing set, entirely painted in light teal.<ref name="JGG" />
